Malad Fish Market is a great place to buy fresh fish at good prices. You can get discounted rates if you buy in bulk, and bargaining skills definitely help here. There’s a wide variety of fresh seafood available, and the quality is good if you choose carefully.

featured_reviews.name: ViSHAL SUTAR
featured_reviews.review_text:
1.	Freshness & Variety
•	Wide range of sea fish and also crabs.  ￼
•	Fish catches are fresh; many comment that it’s among the best places for seafood lovers.  ￼
2.	Value for money / Wholesale rates
•	Prices often more reasonable than smaller local shops, especially if you buy early or in bulk.  ￼
•	Ability to bargain.  ￼
3.	Additional services
•	Fish cleaning / cutting service available. Some vendors provide cleaning without extra cost or for a small charge.  ￼
•	Open long hours—starting early in morning through most of the day.  ￼
4.	Location & accessibility
•	Near Malad Railway Station, so relatively easy for many people to reach.  ￼
5.	Atmosphere
•	“Vibe” of a genuine fish market: lively, bustling; people like the authenticity.

featured_reviews.name: bashir shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
That's wonderful to hear! The Malad Fish Market in Mumbai is indeed very well-known for being a bustling, vibrant hub.
​It's famous for:
​Wholesale and Retail: It's a major market where you can buy a vast variety of fresh saltwater fish at both wholesale and retail prices.

featured_reviews.review_text: It was crowded but not heavily. Ideal timings are 6 to 7 am in the morning you will get fresh catch there. Bargaining doesn't work for me but if you have good bargaining skills you can buy at affordable price.

featured_reviews.name: Sushil Malik
featured_reviews.review_text: Malad Fish Market is a large, busy seafood market in Malad West, just a short walk from Malad railway station (West) on Sainath Road, and is popular for fresh, relatively low-priced sea fish. Location and access Located on Sainath Road, very close to Malad Railway Station (West); it is  2–5 minutes from the station. Timings  roughly 6:00 am onwards; morning hours are the main time when the wholesale and freshest stock comes.Locals recommend going around 6:00–7:30 am if you want the best catch and prices, especially if buying in bulk. Market layout and what you getThe market is divided into multiple sections: unloading/wholesale area on the road, a covered retail area where they also clean and cut, and open sections where you buy and then pay extra at cutting counters. You typically get a wide variety of saltwater fish like pomfret, surmai, bangda, bombil, prawns, crabs and seasonal catch, with both retail and wholesale options. Tips for visiting Go early, carry change, and be ready to bargain hard; prices are better if you buy in larger quantities.It is a traditional wet market, so expect crowds, strong smell, and wet floors. simple washable footwear and carrying your own bags can be more comfortable.If you tell what exactly you want (pomfret, prawns, bulk/retail, specific budget),

featured_reviews.name: Falguni P
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kids Friendly place.
This place is divided into different sections, the entry is free.

*Fish park - this park is quite big and has 3 gates,
The first half has fish tanks, selfie point and a fountain
Currently there are only few fishes, the fountain is shut and the empty tanks are not maintained well (due to COVID)

*The cricket ground - usually there is local cricket match on weekends, chairs are provided for audience.

*Kids play area- there are slides, swings, and play area for kids.

*Open Gym- they have a gym area near the second gate, which is currently closed for public, equipments are mainted nicely.

*Walking / jogging track - there is a long walking and jogging track around the park, local residents usually come visit for morning and evening walks

*Accessibility - park is partially Accessibility as there are stairs in some parts of the park. This place is ideal for kids, family and senior citizens.
The fish park gate is accessible but to reach the other area it is ideal to use the second gate which has a slope.

featured_reviews.name: Prashant.k
featured_reviews.review_text:
The quality has declined; no longer the local gem it used to be.
I am a local here and have been a loyal customer of this restaurant for a very long time. It saddens me to say that they seem to have forgotten their roots. In an effort to increase profit margins, they are clearly cutting corners on quality.
I recently ordered the Pomfret Thali, and the fish fry was a massive disappointment—the plate was literally swimming in oil. Furthermore, they have started charging extra for small things like sonkari, which used to be part of the authentic experience. If you are visiting for the first time, you might not notice, but as someone who knows the original taste, the change is obvious. There are plenty of other great options nearby—I suggest you try those instead.
